[Android] Drop redundant FRE switch from tests (2/10)

Tests that start ChromeTabbedActivity through a CtaTransitTestRule
already mark the first run flow as complete via
FirstRunStatus.setFirstRunFlowComplete(true), both in
ChromeTabbedActivityEntryPoints and in BlankCTATabInitialStateRule.
The other effects of DISABLE_FIRST_RUN_EXPERIENCE in tests
(suppressing the Glic promo and the startup enterprise signals
disclaimer) are now covered by DISABLE_STARTUP_PROMOS, which
ChromeActivityTestRule appends by default. So the switch is redundant
in these tests.

This is a mechanical removal from @CommandLineFlags.Add annotations.
Files are skipped when they also start activities outside of the
transit entry points (e.g. Custom Tabs, webapps, raw intents, direct
ChromeTabbedActivityTestRule start calls, activity restarts), since
those paths may run before FirstRunStatus is set.

The change is split by directory into 10 independent CLs to avoid
constant merge conflicts.

This part: chrome/android/javatests: top level and app.

[BottomSheetTypes] Fix comparator and update bottomsheet tests

Fixes BottomSheetType.compare(a, b) so it returns 0 when two sheets can
both supersede each other (e.g. two user-initiated sheets) instead of
returning -1 in both directions, which violated PriorityQueue's
antisymmetry contract when re-queueing a preempted sheet.

Also adds setSheetType() / getSheetType() to TestBottomSheetContent
(defaulting to a standard BottomSheetType) and updates bottomsheet unit
and instrumentation tests for BottomSheetTypes.

[UOO] Enable UniversalOptOutUpdateOnGeoLocationChanged by default

Flips kUniversalOptOutUpdateOnGeoLocationChanged to
base::FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT so UniversalOptOutService updates
location history and eligibility on OnCountryOrAdminAreaChanged()
notifications (including 304 responses and UTC day rollovers) rather
than waiting for a full 200 variations seed fetch via OnSeedFetched()
(introduced behind the flag in https://crrev.com/c/8640751).

Updates UniversalOptOutServiceTest so legacy OnSeedFetched() and
feature-disabled tests explicitly disable
kUniversalOptOutUpdateOnGeoLocationChanged, while
OnCountryOrAdminAreaChangedUpdatesEligibility exercises the enabled
default directly.

[Contextual Tasks] Use dark mode for incognito panel on Desktop Android

On Desktop Android, the AIM side panel picked light or dark mode from
the WebContents color mode, which follows the app's light/dark setting.
That setting is shared by the regular and incognito tab models, so the
incognito side panel opened in light mode whenever the main window was
in light mode. Desktop always uses dark mode for incognito.

- ShouldUseDarkMode(Profile*) now returns true for off-the-record
  profiles on all platforms.
- Replace ShouldUseDarkMode(Profile*, GURL) with
  ShouldUseDarkMode(WebContents*, GURL), which falls back to the
  WebContents color mode on Android. ContextualTasksUI uses it for both
  the darkMode load-time value and the WebPreferences color scheme,
  removing the per-platform #ifs.
- GetCommonSearchParamsMapForContextualTasks sets cs=1 for incognito on
  Android too.

Desktop behavior is unchanged.

After: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTk0MDE0ODM2MDQ0NTk1MnwzNzQyZjMzMi1hYw

Reland "[UndoTabClosures] Finalize undoable tab closures at close time"

This is a reland of commit 3aacc801b146d12fd4fbd1dfc883c8b3911af0e0

Reland note: The original CL (https://crrev.com/c/8705238) was reverted
due to a compile failure in
TabCollectionTabModelImplUnitTest#createArchivedModel after
TabModelJniBridge.Natives#init migrated to JniUniquePtr, and a test
failure in
RecentlyClosedBridgeTest#testOpenRecentlyClosedTab_FromGroupClosure_CurrentTabDisposition
caused by sorting tabsToClose into model order on !isPendingClosure
(which included allowUndo=false closures). This reland updates
createArchivedModel() to return JniUniquePtr and restricts the
model-order sorting in TabCollectionTabModelImpl#closeTabsInternal to
finalizeUndoableClosure only.

Original change's description:
> [UndoTabClosures] Finalize undoable tab closures at close time
>
> Under kUndoableTabClosureRework, undoable closures in the regular tab
> model are no longer kept pending. They are finalized at close time like
> non-undoable closures: observers are notified while the tabs are still
> in the model (so they are saved to TabRestoreService right away), then
> the tabs are removed and destroyed. The archived tab model keeps pending
> closures for now.
>
> Also:
> - Add a TabModelObserver.onFinishingMultipleTabClosure overload that
>   carries the closing source, undo runnable and close-all state.
> - Report and save closed tabs in model order.
> - Internal commits no longer notify allTabsClosureCommitted when nothing
>   is pending, but commitAllTabClosures() still does under the flag so
>   callers keep dismissing undo snackbars.
> - Keep hidden groups marked as hiding until after didRemoveTabGroup.
> - Don't save collaboration placeholder tabs to recently closed tabs when
>   undoing under the flag.
>
> With the flag disabled, behaviour is unchanged.
>

Filter out feedback metadata when system information is unchecked

The send feedback form currently sends feedback metadata regardless of
whether system information is checked (except on ChromeOS:
https://crrev.com/c/3711138). This CL adds a check to filter out the
EXTRA_DIAGNOSTICS value if system information is left unchecked, so we
don't send this data when the user opts out and have parity with
ChromeOS behavior.

This is to align with privacy requirements for Reading Mode send
feedback (https://crrev.com/c/8666616).

android: Pin Android 17 AVD creation config to emulator 37.1.11

Pin emulator_package in android_37_google_apis_ps16k_x64.textpb
back from 37.2.13 (Stable) to 37.1.11 (Stable) while keeping the
Android 17 QPR2 (37.2 r7) system image.

While emulator 37.2.13 (https://crrev.com/c/8749082) fixed the 37.2.12
host OpenGL ES memory leak (https://issuetracker.google.com/568480829),
it cherry-picked the process-owned GL cleanup change without its
follow-up null-surface check in EglContext::~EglContext(), causing host
qemu-system-x86_64 crashes on ProcessCleanupThread across multi-process
test suites in
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/try/android-17-x64-fyi-rel/208/infra.

Emulator 37.1.11 (currently used on ci/android-17-x64-fyi-rel) predates
both regressions while supporting API 37, Uwb=off, and swangle_indirect.

  kImplicitlyDenied in ContentSettingNotificationsImageModel, and check
  Chrome's origin-level notification permission directly so the expanded
  indicator is shown passively across in-scope navigations and inactive

  changes, and window visibility/activation when an attributed web app
  has Chrome NOTIFICATIONS permission granted while macOS permission is
  kPromptPending or kImplicitlyDenied.

Fix race conditions in InstanceSwitcherCoordinatorTest when renaming
windows. Previously, tests asserted the rename callback synchronously
without waiting for the asynchronous callback and did not wait for
the rename modal dialog to dismiss before matching the underlying
instance switcher dialog root.

Migrate ash system web apps to ApplicationLocaleStorage::GetTag()

ApplicationLocaleStorage::Get() returns the application locale as a
std::string. Migrate the ChromeOS system web apps to GetTag(), which
returns a base::i18n::LanguageTag, so that callers carry the type-safe
locale representation and Get() can eventually be removed.

This is a mechanical, behavior-preserving change: Get() currently returns
exactly std::string(GetTag().tag_string()).

48113bc806a1c39fe4e9b2f1eaee8befb320ba46 [ diff ] 
Reland "[devtools] Add GetBrowserWindowCaptureDevice() for Chrome"

This is a reland of commit 719fb77cad92f8e7f3ac897fb3787734f3c081ef

It was reverted because DevToolsWindowRecordingTest.Resize failed on
linux-wayland-mutter-rel-tests. On Linux with Wayland, the browser
window has a transparent border for the frame shadow. The capture
includes this border, and it is black in the video, so about 10% of the
pixels were black, also before the resize. The test required fewer than
5% black pixels to detect letterbox bars.

Now the test checks the aspect ratio of the last frame instead: it must
match the resized window, and not the initial window. This is what
letterbox bars change, and the frame shadow does not change it. The
recording code does not change.

Original change's description:
> [devtools] Add GetBrowserWindowCaptureDevice() for Chrome
>
> Page.startScreenRecording with captureArea: browserWindow must record
> the browser window that shows the target. Only the embedder knows which
> window that is, so content asks it.
>
> Add DevToolsManagerDelegate::GetBrowserWindowCaptureDevice(). The
> embedder returns a BrowserWindowCaptureDevice: the DesktopMediaID of the
> window, as in a getDisplayMedia() response, and an optional
> MediaStreamUI that shows that the window is captured. The default
> implementation fails, so headless and content_shell return an error, as
> before.
>
> PageHandler asks the delegate for the device, because that decides
> which window the client may record, and starts the recording with
> MediaRecorder::StartDisplayCapture(). Audio comes from the target, as
> when only the target is recorded. If Page.stopScreenRecording runs
> before the embedder answers, it fails, and the start command fails too.
>
> Implement the delegate in Chrome with the parts that getDisplayMedia()
> uses for window capture:
>
> - For a docked DevTools window, use the browser window of the inspected
>   tab, which shows DevTools and the page. An undocked DevTools window is
>   not supported, because the page is in another window. For a tab
>   target, use the browser window of the tab.
> - Respect the ScreenCaptureAllowed policy like getDisplayMedia() window
>   capture. The check uses an empty origin, because a CDP client and not
>   the inspected page asks for the recording. Thus a specific origin in
>   the per-origin lists does not apply, but the "*" pattern does.
> - Create the DesktopMediaID of the browser window like the picker does
>   for Chrome's own windows, so that the launcher uses the viz-based
>   window capture device.
> - Call GetDevicesForDesktopCapture(), which returns the device and a
>   MediaStreamUI that registers with MediaStreamCaptureIndicator and
>   shows the screen sharing notification with a Stop button. The
>   notification names the product, for example "Google Chrome is sharing
>   a window".
>
> The recording shows what the window shows. If the target is in a
> background tab, or if the user selects another tab, the recording shows
> the active tab.
>
> There is no picker and no user activation, because the use case is
> automation over a trusted CDP connection.
>
> The browser tests run on Aura (including ChromeOS) and Mac. They decode
> the recording in a <video> element and check that the video shows the
> whole window with the page for a DevTools target and a tab target (also
> with docked DevTools, which is how a client records the page's audio),
> that the video follows the window size after a resize, that the
> indicator follows the recording, that Stop in the UI (also a click on
> the real Stop button of the notification) stops the capture but keeps
> the stream, the error cases (undocked DevTools, untrusted client,
> policy), and how the per-origin policy lists apply.
> Page.startScreenRecording answers after the first frame, so the tests
> have no fixed waits.
>

parent
3563956c5be6968ac0c96e59903f55d5bb64b319 [ diff ] 
Use the V8 code cache for module scripts on the background response processor path

With BackgroundResourceFetch's background script response processor
(the default since M130), an external module script that had a V8 code
cache never used it: BackgroundJSStreamManager::
MaybeCreateConsumeCodeCacheTask() returned early for module scripts
before setting has_code_cache, so the processor streamed the module
and the main thread compiled it from the streamed source, ignoring the
cache, and then produced and stored a new cache on every load. Classic
scripts were unaffected, and modules used the cache with
background-script-response-processor disabled.

The early return existed because module scripts could not consume a
code cache off the main thread. Now that they can (previous CL), treat
module scripts exactly like classic scripts here: start the
ConsumeCodeCacheTask on the background thread and hand the decoded
source plus the task to the main thread instead of streaming.

Module scripts are always decoded as UTF-8 and their code cache is tagged
with UTF-8 (TextResourceDecoder ignores the charset parameter for
kAlwaysUseUTF8ForText). The background processor applied the response's
charset parameter unconditionally, so for a module served with a
non-UTF-8 charset (or a UTF-16 BOM) it would look for the wrong cache
tag and decode with the wrong encoding; it now takes
TextResource::EncodingIsAlwaysUTF8() into account and builds its
decoders with the same options as the resource.

The module code cache browser test only checked that a cache is
produced; it now loads the page a third time and checks that the module
was compiled with the code cache (this failed for the
BackgroundResourceFetch-enabled variants). Unit tests cover the
background processor's handling of a module script with a code cache.

Linux x64 official build, 25 warm loads (warm HTTP cache, code cache
already produced) of two module-script pages from Speedometer 3's
resources served locally, renderer main thread, mean, before -> after
this and the previous CL:
  NewsSite-Nuxt entry bundle: V8 compile+deserialize during load
    19.0 -> 3.4 ms; navigation to module evaluated 19.2 -> 11.1 ms;
    navigation to load event 69.8 -> 52.2 ms.
  TodoMVC-Angular bundles (3 modules): V8 compile+deserialize
    36.8 -> 2.5 ms; navigation to module evaluated 36.1 -> 26.1 ms;
    navigation to load event 54.4 -> 34.0 ms.
A 1 MB module that executes almost none of its code at load (the worst
case for consuming rather than streaming) keeps its main-thread compile
cost (1.3 -> 1.35 ms) and halves navigation to load event (37 -> 18 ms).

localized strings, blocking cross-platform test execution.

Forward device selection to perf smoke-test subprocesses

The benchmark-list and Telemetry end-to-end smoke tests forward the
browser type to their subprocesses but omit the selected device. When
run with --device=<serial>, the subprocess can discover browsers on
other connected devices instead of preserving the parent selection.

Forward an explicitly configured device in both subprocess commands.
Leave automatic discovery unchanged when no device is specified.

Validation of subprocess arguments covers an Android serial, desktop,
and an unset device for both tests. Android end-to-end validation with
two connected devices is still pending.

Full presubmit is blocked by missing perf validation scripts in the
sparse checkout. Telemetry end-to-end tests have not been run.

Update exclusive access bubble when an OOPIF requests fullscreen again

When a tab is already in fullscreen and a cross-site out-of-process
iframe (OOPIF) requests fullscreen,
FullscreenController::EnterFullscreenModeForTab updates
`requesting_origin_` to the requesting frame's last committed origin,
but previously did not call `ExclusiveAccessManager::UpdateBubble` in
the `was_window_fullscreen_for_tab_or_pending` branch. As a result, the
exclusive access bubble continued displaying the stale origin of the
previous fullscreen requester.

Call `exclusive_access_manager()->UpdateBubble(base::NullCallback())` in
the `was_window_fullscreen_for_tab_or_pending` branch so the bubble
origin is updated whenever a different frame takes over fullscreen.

Verification:
- Repro (Before): ./out/Linux/unit_tests --ozone-platform=headless
  --gtest_filter="FullscreenControllerStateUnitTest.CrossSiteSubframeReentryUpdatesBubbleOrigin"
  -> FAILED (bubble_update_count remained 1 and origin remained
  https://secure.test:8443 instead of https://bank.test:8443)
- Fix (After): ./out/Linux/unit_tests --ozone-platform=headless
  --gtest_filter="FullscreenControllerStateUnitTest.CrossSiteSubframeReentryUpdatesBubbleOrigin"
  -> PASSED (302 ms)
- Regression: ./out/Linux/unit_tests --ozone-platform=headless
  --gtest_filter="FullscreenController*:ExclusiveAccess*" -> 69/69 tests
  passed, 0 failures

[Focus] Animate Tab Group and Container Views From the Focus Mode Motion

Drives focus mode enter and exit transitions from the
FocusModeAnimations::kFocusMode motion started by
TabStripCollectionController:

- TabGroupView subscribes to the focus motion and updates its header,
  Unfocus button, and group line each frame from GetFocusProgress().
- UnpinnedTabContainerView::LayoutManager blends between the unfocused
  and focused layouts during enter and exit so unrelated children shrink
  away and grow back smoothly.
- TabStripCollectionController suppresses secondary layout animations
  while the focus motion runs and holds the model removal lock for
  exiting ephemeral groups until the exit motion completes.

[Contextual Tasks] Attribute pinned button context menu removals correctly

When ContextualTasksPinnedButtonContextMenuCloseSidePanel is enabled, the
permanently pinned Contextual Tasks toolbar button's context menu offers a
"Close/Remove" item. Selecting it called
RemoveEphemeralButtonForCurrentTask(), which always recorded
ContextualTasks.EphemeralToolbarButton.UserAction.RemoveByContextMenu, so
removals from the pinned button were counted as ephemeral button usage.
This happened with and without ContextualTasksEphemeralPinButtonRefactor.

Record a new ContextualTasks.PermanentToolbarButton.UserAction.
RemoveByContextMenu user action and histogram when the button is pinned,
and keep recording the ephemeral metric when it is not.

[metrics] Use constexpr validator tables and filter CrOS projects

structured_metrics_validator previously generated 140 polymorphic
ProjectValidator/EventValidator subclasses, startup Initialize()
methods, and 366 heap-allocated unordered_maps, and compiled all
ChromeOS-only projects into non-ChromeOS builds (~63 KB on arm32).

Emit constexpr sorted .rodata tables with a deduplicated string table
(binary-searched via std::ranges::lower_bound with zero dynamic
relocations or heap allocations), and skip ChromeOS-only projects in
gen_events.py and gen_validator.py when !is_chromeos. This shrinks the
validator footprint on non-ChromeOS arm32 to ~5.5 KB (~58 KB savings)
ahead of enabling Structured Metrics on Android
(https://crrev.com/c/8709543).

[glic] Record UMA histogram for actor task OS notifications

Records Glic{GlicProvider}.Actor.TaskOsNotification.Event in
GlicActorTaskNotificationHandler to track desktop OS-level task-start
notification lifecycle events for experimental triggering actor tasks:
- kShown when display is requested,
- kSkippedBrowserActive when suppressed due to an active browser window,
- kClicked when clicked by the user, and
- kClosed when closed by the user or OS without being clicked.

Tracks currently displayed task IDs on the handler and clears them in
OnClick, OnClose, and Close so programmatic closes (when clicked or when
the task ends) neither emit kClosed on MessageCenter nor leak task IDs.

Add PrefTransformerInterface::IsExtensionModifiable() and implement it
in ProxyOverrideRulesTransformer using
proxy_config::AreUserProxyOverrideRulesAllowed(). Also add
PrefTransformerInterface::Observer and PrefModifiabilityObserver to
support observing dynamic modifiability changes per BrowserContext
(wired up in ProxyOverrideRulesTransformer and PreferenceEventRouter in
the follow-up CL).

When user-scoped/extension-controlled ProxyOverrideRules are not allowed
(because the user is unaffiliated on a managed desktop device and
EnableProxyOverrideRulesForAllUsers is not enabled):
- preference_helpers::GetLevelOfControl() reports "not_controllable".
- SetPreferenceFunction::Run() rejects the set() call with an error and
  does not persist the value in ExtensionPrefs.

[Android] Fix bottom bar crash when toggled during recreation

Turning the Toolbar setting off and on again in quick succession can
crash Chrome. The first toggle recreates the tabbed activity without
the bottom bar. If the second toggle lands before that activity
finishes native initialization, startup tries to build the bottom bar
without the objects it depends on.

Build the bottom bar from the state captured when the activity was
created, so a later toggle only triggers another recreation.

Inline ExternalCanvasResource dtor into callback.

Callback is sole owner of the resource, so when we leave scope, dtor
always run. If we're in cross thread path, then it's no op and callback
doesn't run.

If not, then we run ExternalCanvasResource's callback.

[iOS][AuroraAIM] Surface AIM Tile on Cold Start

On cold start, MostVisitedTilesMediator initializes and receives initial
tiles via -mostVisitedSites:didUpdateTiles: before TemplateURLService
and AimEligibilityService finish loading asynchronously. Because
AIModeButtonServiceIOS::IsButtonAvailable() initially returns false, the
initial Most Visited Tiles list is built without the virtual AI Mode
tile. When AIModeButtonServiceIOS later becomes available and triggers
-updateAIMAvailability, relying on MostVisitedSites::RefreshTiles()
fails to surface the tile if a TopSites query is already in flight
(InitiateTopSitesQuery() early-returns when weak pointers are active).

Ensure the virtual AI Mode tile surfaces reliably on cold start as soon
as AIModeButtonServiceIOS becomes available:
- Cache the latest NTPTilesVector in MostVisitedTilesMediator when
  -mostVisitedSites:didUpdateTiles: is invoked.
- Extract -buildMostVisitedItemsFromTiles: to synchronously rebuild
  MostVisitedItems and update the consumer from the cached tiles when
  -updateAIMAvailability or -undoUnpinAIMTileWithIndex: runs, removing
  redundant RefreshTiles() calls.
- Record Omnibox.AimEntrypoint.Shown when AI Mode availability changes
  after the initial tile impression.

[DW] Read caption bar insets and bounding rects ignoring visibility

On desktop devices, fullscreen windows report an invisible caption bar
until the app opts into header customization. Update caption bar inset
observation to read caption bar insets and bounding rects ignoring
visibility so Chrome can customize the fullscreen app header on launch.

Core changes:
* Add a helper in WindowInsetsUtils to read bounding rects ignoring
  visibility.
* Add a protected hook in InsetsRectProvider to read insets for the
  observed type and clear ignoring-visibility insets when consumed.
* Update CaptionBarInsetsRectProvider to read caption bar insets and
  bounding rects ignoring visibility while the status bar or caption
  bar is visible, falling back to visible insets in immersive mode.

[MemoryCoordinator] Introduce base::MemoryPressureSource

base::MemoryPressureListener is deprecated and will be removed in favor
of base::MemoryConsumer. However, the memory pressure signal is still
needed, both as an input to the memory coordinator policies and for
metrics. It is currently held by MemoryPressureListenerRegistry, which
will be removed along with MemoryPressureListener.

MemoryPressureSource takes over that role: it holds the process's memory
pressure level and notifies its subscribers. Suppression and simulation
move over unchanged, and MemoryPressureListenerRegistry now subscribes
to the source to keep serving the remaining listeners. All owners of the
registry now create the source right before it.

Also add ScopedMemoryPressureLevelOverride, a test helper meant to
replace SimulatePressureNotification() in tests that don't own the
source (e.g. browser tests).

Behavior change: a MemoryPressureListener that registers while
notifications are suppressed now starts at the last notified level
rather than the real one.

Revert "Roll Fuchsia SDK from 34.20261029.4.1 to 34.20261105.6.1"

This reverts commit 766e3622b5d3f7bc660e30da69858b41c59e8a54.

Reason for revert: since this roll landed, fuchsia-x64-cast-receiver-rel
has been failing almost every build. Test shards running on the Fuchsia
emulator lose the device after 4-7 minutes:

  Transport error: Connection to the device has been lost
  There was an internal error running tests:
      Fidl(ClientRead(Other(Transport(None))))
  [Forwarded(SSH stderr: Timeout, server 127.0.0.1 not responding.)]

This mostly hits content_browsertests, where 2-8 shards fail per build
and some still fail after retry. It also hits
pixel_skia_gold_passthrough_test, context_lost_passthrough_tests,
headless_browsertests and web_engine_browsertests. Different tests are
running each time the device is lost, and the failing shards are spread
across e2 and e4 bots in several zones. Before the roll (build 32061 and
earlier) content_browsertests had no failed shards.

The roll's Cq-Include-Trybots did not cover this x64 builder, and
content_browsertests only runs on CI there, so CQ did not catch it.

Revert to the previous SDK version until the emulator issue is
understood.

First failing build:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/fuchsia-x64-cast-receiver-rel/32062

[Clank] Add TabBottomSheet hooks for content overlays

Add hooks so TabBottomSheetContent subclasses can mount overlays on
the sheet:
- TabBottomSheetCoordinator sends the container bottom margin to
  TabBottomSheetContent.onBottomMarginChanged() when the sheet opens
  and when the margin changes.
- TabBottomSheetCoordinator.createSheetContent() destroys any
  previous mSheetContent before it creates another. When
  BottomSheetController hides a queued sheet, it skips destroy(),
  which previously leaked the old content on the next show.
- TabBottomSheetUtils exposes getExpandedContentGroup() and
  getWebUiContainer() for overlay views.

Existing behavior does not change for current callers.

[Android] Drop redundant FRE switch from tests (4/10)

Tests that start ChromeTabbedActivity through a CtaTransitTestRule
already mark the first run flow as complete via
FirstRunStatus.setFirstRunFlowComplete(true), both in
ChromeTabbedActivityEntryPoints and in BlankCTATabInitialStateRule.
The other effects of DISABLE_FIRST_RUN_EXPERIENCE in tests
(suppressing the Glic promo and the startup enterprise signals
disclaimer) are now covered by DISABLE_STARTUP_PROMOS, which
ChromeActivityTestRule appends by default. So the switch is redundant
in these tests.

This is a mechanical removal from @CommandLineFlags.Add annotations.
Files are skipped when they also start activities outside of the
transit entry points (e.g. Custom Tabs, webapps, raw intents, direct
ChromeTabbedActivityTestRule start calls, activity restarts), since
those paths may run before FirstRunStatus is set.

The change is split by directory into 10 independent CLs to avoid
constant merge conflicts.

27cac8fef16505965e5beba83948edd74cb50d5d [ diff ] 
[glic] Recover experimental triggering from early guest reloads

When the Glic `<webview>` reloads or executes an initial SPA route/auth
redirect right after `InvokeWithAutoSubmit` succeeds—before the web
client has sent any response or worklog—the `ExperimentalTriggering`
Mojo pipes drop and previously caused `ExperimentalTriggeringUpdatesHandler`
to immediately emit `Client disconnected unexpectedly.`. Additionally,
`GlicExperimentalTriggeringManager::client_` lacked a disconnect handler
or `WrapCallbackWithDefaultInvokeIfNotRun` wrapper on
`GetExperimentalTriggeringUpdates`, leaving stale bound state if the web
client disconnected mid-registration.

Fix both issues:
1. Reset `GlicExperimentalTriggeringManager::client_` on Mojo disconnect,
   wrap `GetExperimentalTriggeringUpdates` with default `false` invoke on
   pipe drop, and expose `IsClientBound()` + `AddClientBoundCallback()`.
2. Gate `ExperimentalTriggeringUpdatesHandler` behind a 10s reconnect
   grace window (`kGlicExperimentalTriggeringNavigationReconnectGrace`,
   enabled by default) when the updates pipe disconnects before
   `first_response_received_`. When the reloaded guest re-binds
   `ExperimentalTriggeringClient`, re-subscribe `receiver_` and re-invoke
   `InvokeWithAutoSubmit` targeting `instance_->id()` with
   `supersede_if_in_progress = true` (at most once per turn).

Reland "[GCM] Clear pending InstanceID token callbacks in Stop"

This is a reland of commit 37e7604f8a0dfcb192cb554d78616aec35aa61f5

Synchronously invoking pending token callbacks in
`GCMDriverDesktop::Stop()` caused re-entrancy crashes during teardown in
callers that do not invalidate weak pointers before calling
`RemoveAppHandler()` (crbug.com/582169559, crbug.com/582637002). Clear
`get_token_callbacks_` and `delete_token_callbacks_` silently in
`Stop()` instead.

Original change's description:
> [GCM] Clear pending InstanceID token callbacks in Stop
>
> GCMDriverDesktop::RemoveCachedData invalidates weak pointers when the
> service stops, cancelling pending UI callbacks from IOWorker, while
> ClearCallbacks only cleared legacy register, unregister, and send maps.
> Any in-flight InstanceID token operation left its entry in
> get_token_callbacks_ or delete_token_callbacks_ permanently, causing
> subsequent token requests to fail with ASYNC_OPERATION_PENDING. Invoke
> pending token callbacks with GCM_DISABLED in Stop().
>

[tab_bottom_sheet] Support loading placeholder view in CoBrowseViews.

Android bottom-sheet and side-panel embedders built on `CoBrowseViews`
currently only swap between the live `WebContents` container and an
empty/inactive placeholder view, with no slot for a native loading
skeleton while the web client initializes.

Add optional native loading placeholder support to `CoBrowseViews` and
`CoBrowseViewsBridge`. Expose a default `createLoadingPlaceholderView`
hook on `CoBrowseComponentProvider` (returning `null` for existing
callers), host the view in a predefined `loading_placeholder_container`
in `tab_bottom_sheet.xml`, and route its close button through a
`Runnable` that `CoBrowseViewFactory` adapts from the native
`CoBrowseViewsBridge` and that becomes a no-op after `destroy()`.

Add `CoBrowseViews.setIsLoading(boolean)` and
`CoBrowseViewsBridge::SetIsLoading(bool)` (preserved across view
rebuilds). While loading, the placeholder covers `web_ui_container`
(`INVISIBLE`, preserving layout bounds) even if a `WebContents` is
attached, and suppresses `empty_placeholder_container` (`GONE`).

[iOS][STTS] Retry omnibox IPH on later triggers

Previously, the browser agent stopped attempting the Send Tab to Self
omnibox IPH after the first eligible page, even if presentation was
blocked (for example, by an active banner or before the feature
engagement tracker finished initializing).

Rely on the feature engagement tracker to cap presentation instead of a
separate one-shot flag, and check whether the tracker would trigger
before computing page eligibility on each attempt.

[ASI] Add a bubble that points at the Settings "Set default" button

AnnotatedSetterBubbleControllerWin finds the Windows Settings window,
measures the "Set default" button through
SettingsRowLocatorWin::MeasureButton(), and keeps an
AnnotatedSetterBubble anchored to it. Measurement follows the visual
guide's arrow: nothing is shown until the button is measured, a resize
re-measures after 300 ms, stale and superseded replies are dropped, and
three failures in a row end the guidance. Unlike the arrow, a failure is
retried, since nothing is shown otherwise. The Settings process is held
once found, and the window's owner is checked before each measurement
and on every change.

The Settings window is never moved or resized. The bubble is an inactive
top-level widget that follows the window, hides while it is minimized,
and closes when the window is destroyed, hidden or cloaked. Its title
carries the Google G (the product logo in Chromium builds).

Nothing uses the controller yet; a setter does in a follow-up.

[Menus] Target touch gestures at the touch point

When a user taps a button inside a views menu with a finger, views
expands the tap into a bounding box around the finger's center point and
picks whichever child view has at least 60% of its own area covered and
has its center closest to the touch point. Because tiny decorative views
(such as a 16x16 row icon above or scrolled behind the pinned footer, or
a 1x24 separator next to the zoom buttons) are much smaller than an
83x26 footer button, a tap on the left half of the Settings button is
closer to the adjacent row icon's center than to the wide button's own
center, and covers 100% of the icon while covering less than 60% of the
button. The decorative view wins targeting and ignores the tap, and the
menu controller (which checks only the center point of the tap) sees
only the non-activating container row and drops the tap.

Target menu gestures using the 1x1 rect at the finger's center point,
which selects views' point-based targeting path (matching mouse clicks
and the menu controller's own gesture handling for standard menu rows).
Any tap whose finger center lands anywhere inside a menu button now
activates that button directly instead of being stolen by a nearby icon
or separator.

[Menus] Make gesture tap use the mouse-release row activation gate

A finger tap that no child view handled could activate a menu row that
only hosts child controls. A mouse click on the same spot is ignored.
In the ChroMenu app menu, taps that land in the gaps between the top
block buttons or the footer buttons hit this case. Those container rows
use command id 0, which is Cut, so the menu closed and ran Cut instead
of the button the user aimed at. Real fingers hit those gaps some of
the time, so taps seemed to fail at random.

Mouse release and gesture tap now share one activation check, so the
pointer type no longer changes whether a row activates.

Rows whose body is meant to activate opt in:
- Birch bar switch and checkbox rows. This restores the tap behavior
  that crrev.com/c/8640331 broke and that got it reverted.
- App menu rows with a chip.

Intended behavior changes:
- Mouse: a click on a Birch row's label or padding now toggles the
  row, the same as a tap. A click on the control itself is unchanged.
- Mouse: a click on a chip row now runs its action. It used to do
  nothing.
- Touch: a tap on a disabled zoom +/- button, or on the zoom row label,
  keeps the menu open, the same as a click.
- Touch: a tap on the currently selected desk profile row (the one with
  the checkmark) keeps the menu open instead of closing it. That row
  does not opt in; selecting it again is a no-op, and a click there
  already did nothing.

[TabUI Virtualization] Insert provider items at their anchor

When TabListMediator is backed by a TabListDataProvider, the provider
reports new tabs, and groups expanding into their member tabs, through
onItemsInserted. That callback was still a stub, so inserted items were
ignored.

The mediator now places the new cards right after the anchor item the
provider names, or at the start of the tab cards when there is none, and
adds them in one provider update so the layout only refreshes once.

If the anchor has no card, the provider and the list are out of sync.
Debug builds assert, and release builds skip the insert instead of
guessing a position.

Provider mode is not wired to any surface yet, so there is no change in
production.

[Android] Drop redundant FRE switch from tests (5/10)

Tests that start ChromeTabbedActivity through a CtaTransitTestRule
already mark the first run flow as complete via
FirstRunStatus.setFirstRunFlowComplete(true), both in
ChromeTabbedActivityEntryPoints and in BlankCTATabInitialStateRule.
The other effects of DISABLE_FIRST_RUN_EXPERIENCE in tests
(suppressing the Glic promo and the startup enterprise signals
disclaimer) are now covered by DISABLE_STARTUP_PROMOS, which
ChromeActivityTestRule appends by default. So the switch is redundant
in these tests.

This is a mechanical removal from @CommandLineFlags.Add annotations.
Files are skipped when they also start activities outside of the
transit entry points (e.g. Custom Tabs, webapps, raw intents, direct
ChromeTabbedActivityTestRule start calls, activity restarts), since
those paths may run before FirstRunStatus is set.

The change is split by directory into 10 independent CLs to avoid
constant merge conflicts.

This part: chrome/android/javatests: payments.

[iOS] Stop NewTabPageMediator bottom omnibox pref observer on shutdown

It seems that _bottomOmniboxEnabled was never stopped. Which mean that
its `_pref` was only released when the pref observer is deallocated.
Best practice requires to stop it explicitly.

The observation was added in https://crrev.com/c/7808304. That CL does
not seem to indicate why it was not reset.

An extra safety could be to have `PrefBackedBoolean` check at dealloc
that `_pref` is nil. This CL does not do it as it seems credible that
more similar issue persists in the codebase currently.

Reland "Enable startup optimization field trial testing configs"

This is a reland of commit 11df5a067d538f1ebad492e15862fb15d731e0f7.

Original change was reverted because enabling
`GtkPrefetchNavButtonIcons`
(`gtk_icon_info_load_symbolic_for_context_async`) triggered a
ThreadSanitizer false positive on `Linux TSan Tests` in
`SingleClientThemesSyncTest` / `TwoClientThemesSyncTest`. When GTK3
loads symbolic icons asynchronously on a GLib `GTask` worker thread,
`gdk-pixbuf` decodes the icon buffer on the worker thread and hands the
`GdkPixbuf*` back to the main thread via `GTask`'s internal `GMutex` in
uninstrumented `libgio`/`libglib`, where
`gtk_icon_info_load_symbolic_finish` unrefs it (`gdk_pixbuf_finalize` in
`libgdk_pixbuf-2.0.so.0`). While `build/sanitizers/tsan_suppressions.cc`
already suppresses `libgio*.so`, `libglib*.so`, and `libgobject*.so`,
`g_object_unref` tail-calls `gdk_pixbuf_finalize` in
`libgdk_pixbuf-2.0.so.0` (and `gdk-pixbuf >= 2.43` uses `libglycin.so`
worker threads). Add `libgdk_pixbuf*.so` and `libglycin*.so` to the
uninstrumented system library list in `tsan_suppressions.cc`.

856d812a1e37e5db555e8ee6105250bee83b7cd2 [ diff ] 
[TabUI Virtualization] Refresh provider cards in place on data reset

When TabListMediator is backed by a TabListDataProvider, every data
reset cleared and rebuilt all tab cards, even when the tab switcher was
reopened over the same tabs. That drops each card's model, so thumbnails
refetch and the list relayouts, and the quickMode hint from
resetWithListOfTabs was ignored.

The legacy path already avoids this with areTabsUnchanged, so provider
mode now does the same: if the snapshot lists the same tabs and groups
in the same order as the cards on screen, each card is updated where it
is and quickMode is passed through. Otherwise the cards are rebuilt as
before.

In the NESTED layout a group header no longer observes its member tabs.
Expanded members are observed through their own cards, and the header
shows no per-tab state, so those observers only did extra work.

Provider mode is not wired to any surface yet, so there is no change in
production.

7590cea5be4641d452f4219ec142ab2d0a9c0b98 [ diff ] 
[Glic] Support explicit actor surface targets for invocations

A Glic invocation needs to target a headless surface for actuation.
Currently, an invocation can set its actuation target only to a
mojom::ActuationTarget value. For kTargetSurface, Chrome can send only
the invoked tab's ID to the web client, as actuation_tab_id.

This CL lets an invocation target an explicit actor surface, such as a
headless surface:

- Target::actuation_target in GlicInvokeOptions can now hold either a
  mojom::ActuationTarget or an actor::ActorSurfaceHandle.

- Chrome sends an explicit surface to the web client as kTargetSurface,
  with the surface ID in actuation_tab_id. For the kTargetSurface enum
  value, Chrome now sends the invoked tab's surface ID instead of its
  tab ID. The two IDs are equal while kUseTabHandleAsSurfaceHandle is
  enabled (the default).

- If the explicit surface does not belong to the invoked tab, Chrome
  does not mark the invoked tab as pending actuation.

- Add a "Use Headless Page" option to chrome://glic/internals for
  kTargetSurface. The option creates a headless surface and passes its
  handle to the invocation. The next headless invocation, or leaving the
  page, destroys the surface.

- Add browser tests for surface ID forwarding, the pending-actuation
  state, and the internals option, including headless surface teardown.

[iOS] Fix the bug that regular profile/browser is returned in empty incognito tab grid.

In the existing code, it uses `incognitoState.incognitoContentVisible`
to determine if it's currently in incognito mode. This causes issue when
there is no tabs in the incognito tab grid and will return the regular
browser or profile since `incognitoContentVisible = NO` in empty
incognito tab grid
https://crsrc.org/c/ios/chrome/browser/tab_switcher/ui_bundled/tab_grid/tab_grid_view_controller.mm;l=1128-1130.

Update it to use `tabGridState.currentPage == TabGridPageIncognitoTabs`
instead to determine if it's in incognito mode. Also adding observing
for `willChangePageTo` because `willEnterIncognitoForState` will not be
fired when entering an empty incognito tab grid
https://crsrc.org/c/ios/chrome/browser/shared/coordinator/scene/state/incognito_state.mm;l=96-98.

Use well-formed MTC CA keys in tests

Tests used to create MTC CA trust anchors and signer set issuers with
fake keys that are not SubjectPublicKeyInfos, since the key was only
parsed when verifying a signature. To prepare for a BoringSSL change to
bssl::MTCAnchor that will reject such keys, this CL switches tests to
use a proper SPKI instead.

Wrap calls to platform notification service into a router function

This change prepares for further changes related to crbug.com/576760752,
and is part of crrev.com/c/8726991 that is big and was suggested to be
split.

The platform notification service is obtained in a number of locations

direct calls with calls to that new function.

No changes to logic and behaviour are intended.

ttc: Ignore non-normal browser windows for voice plate and focus

TTC's page context and tools act on the user's tabbed window, so the
voice plate and VoiceFocusedContentsTracker shouldn't follow app, popup
or devtools windows when they activate. Restrict both to TYPE_NORMAL
windows via ProfileBrowserCollection::FindTabbedBrowser(), which also
skips windows on other workspaces (other desks on ChromeOS).

When the plate's window closes, move the plate straight to the next
tabbed window instead of waiting for one to activate, so it doesn't
vanish while a popup is in front. Skip that move during shutdown so
closing all windows doesn't recreate the plate in each one.

11aaac166e39cf17abaff52da969b8ee357a2823 [ diff ] 
Delay NotifyResourceLost to dtor

For CanvasResourceSharedImage, IsLost is checked in 4 places, but
VideoFrameAcceleratedSnapshotPool is not relevant, as it never uses
ExportedCanvasResource [1].

Two are happening during OnRefReturned [2][3] that comes through
`DropRefOnOwningThread` [4] and also check HasOneRef(). If
`DropRefOnOwningThread` is called by someone else and not
ExportedCanvasResource we will always have more than 1 ref (1 in
ExportedCanvasResource and 1 in callback), so IsLost() check doesn't
matter.

For ShouldReplaceTargetBuffer [5] it's similar, if the resource is
Exported, we have at least two refs, one is `resource()`, one is in
ExportedCanvasResource and so IsLost() check is irrelevant, as the
function will always return true.

One caveat above is that now we will potentially call
NotifyFlushForImage [6] if ShouldReplaceTargetBuffer will happen in
between of display compositor reporting resource lost and dtor of
ExportedCanvasResource. In practice this is practically impossible to
happen, because display compositor needs to be destroyed for it to
happen and our CompositorFrameSink (and so CanvasResourceDispatcher)
needs to destroyed. But even if there is edge case where it's possible,
it would just flush some 2d canvas sooner.

This means that we can delay `NotifyResourceLost()` in
ExportedCanvsResource right until we're about to call
`DropRefOnOwningThread`.

[1]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/video_frame_image_util.cc;drc=2ccb38275c701eee9fc2c4e27b6b01f49bda8eaa;l=290
[2]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_2d_resource_provider.cc;drc=2ccb38275c701eee9fc2c4e27b6b01f49bda8eaa;l=117
[3]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_non_2d_resource_provider.cc;drc=2ccb38275c701eee9fc2c4e27b6b01f49bda8eaa;l=435
[4]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_resource.cc;drc=2ccb38275c701eee9fc2c4e27b6b01f49bda8eaa;l=75
[5]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_non_2d_resource_provider.cc;drc=2ccb38275c701eee9fc2c4e27b6b01f49bda8eaa;l=459
[6]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/graphics/canvas_non_2d_resource_provider.cc;drc=1c199fcf4e3ef04016b0153ac614f431d62a58b4;l=425

[ContextualTasks] Fix mock composebox handler race

UpdateActiveTabContextStatusOnTabSwitch installed a mock composebox
handler via ContextualTasksUI::SetComposeboxHandlerForTesting() right
after opening and closing the side panel. On slow and debug bots, the
cached WebUI finished initializing <cr-composebox> asynchronously later
and called CreatePageHandler(), overwriting owned_composebox_handler_
with a production handler and destroying the test mock before
tab-switch expectations ran.

Store test handlers in a dedicated composebox_handler_for_testing_ slot
so owned_composebox_handler_ keeps the WebUI's Mojo pipes serviced
while composebox_handler_ stays bound to the injected mock across
CreatePageHandler(), await initial WebUI load completion in the test,
and re-enable UpdateActiveTabContextStatusOnTabSwitch.

Add unit test coverage in FullscreenSigninMediatorTest for
- initial load
- sync-disabled subtitle
- reset() after sign-in
- dismiss while signed in
- automotive device lock

have thorough testing before migrating to a new finite state machine
Mediator.

[contextual-tasks]: Remove cr-composebox resize events

The Contextual Tasks wrapper now uses the forked inner composebox and
Lens installs its own ResizeObservers, so `composebox-resize` and
`observeResize` are unused on cr-composebox. Remove them, plus the
observers and overrides that only served them; the fork's event stays.

NO_IFTTT=no logic added to composebox

[Memory Coordinator] Remember memory limit in TestMemoryConsumerRegistry

TestMemoryConsumerRegistry did not remember the limit passed to
NotifyUpdateMemoryLimit(), so consumers registered afterwards started at
the default limit. This differs from the production registries and the
legacy MemoryPressureListenerRegistry, and made tests of a consumer's
initial state pass vacuously.

[policy] Add UMA for non-Chrome namespace merging

MergePolicyBundles() reads the merge metapolicies from the Chrome
namespace but applies the mergers to every namespace, so extension
policies set from several sources are merged too. To decide whether to
restrict merging to the Chrome policies, measure how often that would
change an effective policy value.

Enterprise.PolicyMerge.NonChromeNamespace.ValueChanged.{List,Dictionary}
is recorded by the profile-level PolicyService for each
POLICY_SOURCE_MERGED entry outside the Chrome namespace, when the entry
first appears and whenever its merge result changes: whether the merged
value differs from the one precedence alone would have selected.

[ContextualTasks] Deflake Voice SurfaceAndStartup

ContextualTasksComposeboxForkVoiceTest SurfaceAndStartup enters voice
search mode in its final test, starting requestAnimationFrame loops on
<recording-wave>, <audio-wave>, and <search-animated-glow>. Because
teardown() did not clear document.body, those animation loops continued
executing under V8 block coverage instrumentation and timed out DevTools
JS coverage collection on Linux.

Clear document.body in teardown() so voice animation elements disconnect
before coverage collection, install TestToolbarBrowserProxy and flush
the initial searchbox input state in setup(), and re-enable both
Composebox_Voice_SurfaceAndStartup suites on Linux.

[iOS] Stop `OmniboxMediator` `PlaceholderService` observer

When the mediator’s PlaceholderService is set it observes the service.
It thus is important to set the service back to nil to stop the
observation and avoid retaining a service after the coordinator is
stopped.

The observation was added in https://crrev.com/c/6597066. That CL does
not seem to indicate why it was not reset.

Mark BiDi Bluetooth wdspec tests flaky on Linux

crrev.com/c/8416585 added a browser-side transient activation check to
WebBluetoothServiceImpl::RequestDevice(). The renderer reports the
activation over LocalFrameHost, but sends RequestDevice() on the
separate WebBluetoothService pipe. The two pipes have no ordering
guarantee, so the browser can handle the request first and reject it
with "Must be handling a user gesture to show a permission request."

Every BiDi Bluetooth wdspec test that calls requestDevice() with
script.callFunction(userActivation: true) hits this race, and several
are among the top web test flakes. The tests are correct. The product
fix (crbug.com/577081408) will send RequestDevice() on the same channel
as the activation update. That fix will remove these entries.

This also moves the two existing crbug.com/575786126 entries to
crbug.com/577081408, because 575786126 is a duplicate of it.
simulate_descriptor_response/invalid.py now fails fast instead of
timing out, so it also expects Failure.

[Facilitated Payments] Classify payment QR codes by scheme

Adds `get_payment_qr_code_scheme()`, an EMV Merchant-Presented Mode
validator that:
- Parses the root data objects and verifies the CRC-16 (ID 63).
- Finds the first merchant account information template (IDs 26 to 51)
  whose Globally Unique Identifier is supported, compared
  case-insensitively:
  - Pix (static or dynamic): `br.gov.bcb.pix`.
  - DuitNow: `A0000006150001`.
  - PromptPay: `A000000677010111`.
  - QRIS: any identifier starting with `ID.CO.`, which covers both the
    national `ID.CO.QRIS.WWW` template and the issuer templates, whose
    identifiers are the issuers' reverse domain names.
- Returns `NotPaymentCode`, `UnsupportedScheme`, `FailedTlvParsing`,
  `FailedCrcCheck` or `EmptyAdditionalDataFieldTemplate` otherwise.
It reuses the existing data object parser, and is covered by a new fuzz
test. The validation runs in the browser process; the Rule of Two is
satisfied because the parser is memory-safe Rust.

`get_pix_qr_code_type()` is unchanged. Two seeds of its fuzz test,
which its domain cannot produce and FuzzTest skipped with a warning, are
removed; the unit tests still cover them.

A follow-up CL will validate the QR codes decoded by payment QR code
detection with this function, and log the scheme in opportunity sizing
metrics.

[Clank] Add fallback tests for Omnibox minimization

Behind ClankOmniboxMinimization, keeping the Omnibox hidden during a
same-origin navigation also hides the loading progress bar. To prevent
slow loads from appearing frozen, the Omnibox falls back to SHOWN after
fallback_show_after_ms (counted from the first overlapping navigation)
or when the tab is hidden mid-load.

Add unit tests ahead of the implementation:
- Slow-load and hidden-tab fallback tests need the fallback logic
  (crbug.com/579544014) and are disabled with that bug until it lands,
  alongside an enabled guardrail verifying standalone aborted
  navigations do not trigger a late fallback lock.
- A guardrail test checks that a navigation starting while an editable
  node has focus still takes the load lock. The landed minimization
  skeleton (crrev.com/c/8705274) does not check tab-state locks yet, so
  it is disabled with crbug.com/579544435 until that check lands.

Part of the pre-implementation test stack for crbug.com/578150286.

Update MetadataWriter::BindValues to use base::span

CustomInput is marked STACK_ALLOCATED(), which makes BindValue
(std::pair<BindValueType, CustomInput>) a stack-allocated wrapper type.
Previously, MetadataWriter::BindValues was aliased to
std::vector<BindValue>. This meant that passing bind values to
MetadataWriter::AddSqlFeature placed STACK_ALLOCATED() objects inside a
heap-backed container, requiring STACK_ALLOCATED_IGNORE suppressions.

This change updates BindValues to alias base::span<const BindValue>
instead, as AddSqlFeature only reads the bind values without taking
ownership. This keeps the elements on the stack and allows removing the
STACK_ALLOCATED_IGNORE suppressions in MetadataWriter and
SqlFeatureProcessorTest.

NO_IFTTT=generate_histogram_list.py only parses UMA feature helpers, not BindValues

[rust] Reject `crate_name` in first-party Chromium Rust GN targets.

Before this CL, `rust_static_library`, `rust_macro`,
`rust_shared_library`, and `rust_bindgen` accepted `crate_name` from
any caller.

After this CL, setting `crate_name` in these templates is a GN error in
Chromium builds (`build_with_chromium`), unless the target is in
`third_party` code (other than `//third_party/blink`) or in a few big
`DEPS`-ed directories (`//v8`, `//clank`, `//internal`,
`//ios_internal`).  First-party code should use the default crate name
and `chromium::import!`, or `unsafe_globally_unique_crate_name` in rare
cases.  Projects that reuse `//build` outside of Chromium (e.g. V8,
PDFium, Open Screen) are not affected.

This CL also switches `//build/rust/crubit:cpp_std` (the only remaining
first-party user of `crate_name`) to
`unsafe_globally_unique_crate_name`.

omnibox: Fix the shared WebUI popup prewarm tests

SeveralWindowsPrewarmOnePopup and SkipsPrewarmAfterFirstFrame expected
that a new browser window has no popup content. Since
crrev.com/c/8697556, a window that becomes active takes the idle popup
of another window of the profile, so a new window can hold the first
window's popup, depending on when its activation is handled. The tests
failed on Mac and ChromeOS builders and were disabled there.

Check what the tests are about instead: no window creates its own
popup. A window's popup is either missing or the first window's, as
SkipsPrewarm already checks. Re-enable both tests on Mac and ChromeOS.

Reland "viz: Don't propose the same rounded-display mask candidate twice"

This is a reland of commit 5d3262a53d11c7ec249148a07751185d83dcc04a

The original CL was reverted because its new death test,
ListContainerDeathTest.EraseFromEmptyInnerListDies, failed on Linux
MSan (crbug.com/564188297). The test erased a polymorphic
DerivedElement1 twice. Since
ListContainer::EraseAndInvalidateAllPointers() runs the element's
destructor before ListContainerHelper's checks, the second erase made a
virtual call through the vptr of the already destroyed element. MSan's
use-after-dtor check reported that as use-of-uninitialized-value
("Virtual table ptr was destroyed") before the new CHECK was reached,
so the process did not die with "Check failed".

Changes since the original CL:
- Rebase onto https://crrev.com/c/8452585, which made
  ListContainerHelper use offsets instead of raw pointers.
  InnerList::Erase() now CHECKs the offset against LastElementOffset().
  The old CHECK_GE(position, Begin()) has no offset equivalent, since
  offsets are unsigned.
- Use the trivially destructible NonDerivedElement in the death tests,
  so the second erase doesn't run a destructor on a destroyed object.
- Leave spare capacity in the inner list in the death tests. Otherwise,
  dereferencing the stale iterator hits the DCHECK that
  https://crrev.com/c/8452585 added to InnerList::ElementAtOffset()
  before the CHECK, and EXPECT_CHECK_DEATH() doesn't match the
  "DCHECK failed" message in DCHECK-enabled builds.
- Add death tests for erasing from an inner list that was emptied while
  the container still has elements, and for erasing past the last
  element, to cover the other new CHECKs.

Original change's description:
> viz: Don't propose the same rounded-display mask candidate twice
>
> MaybeAppendOccludingMaskCandidates() appends a proposed candidate that
> carries rounded-display masks to the test candidate list once for every
> candidate already in that list that it occludes. A single mask quad can
> occlude more than one candidate - e.g. a strip across the top of the
> display whose two corner mask squares each intersect a different
> promoted SingleOnTop candidate - so the same proposed candidate, with
> the same QuadList iterator, is appended twice.
>
> If the hardware then accepts the proposed plane set, both copies are
> committed. The commit loop in AttemptMultipleOverlays() sorts candidates
> by descending quad index and commits them back to front so that erasing
> a quad cannot invalidate the iterators of the candidates that follow.
> Two copies of the same candidate defeat that: they share one quad index,
> so OverlayStrategySingleOnTop::CommitCandidate() calls
> QuadList::EraseAndInvalidateAllPointers() twice on the same position.
>
> The second erase runs against an inner list that the first one already
> emptied. cc::ListContainerHelper's InnerList::Erase() computes
>
>   std::copy(position + step, End(), position)
>
> with End() == position, so the length underflows to ~2^64 bytes and the
> copy becomes a wild forward memmove over the heap of the GPU process.
> AddressSanitizer reports it as negative-size-param on the memmove;
> without ASan it linearly overwrites the heap until it reaches an
> unmapped page. It also decrements InnerList::size and ::capacity below
> zero, wrapping the container's bookkeeping.
>
> Fix the root cause: stop scanning once a mask candidate has been found
> to occlude something, so each mask candidate is proposed, tested and
> committed at most once. Whether a mask candidate is appended does not
> depend on how many candidates it occludes, only on whether it occludes
> any, so this does not change which candidates are promoted.
>
> Also harden cc::ListContainerHelper so that a future caller hits a
> controlled crash instead of corrupting the heap. InnerList::Erase()'s
> bounds checks were DCHECKs, which are compiled out in release builds
> where this bug reproduces, so upgrade them to CHECKs and add an explicit
> non-empty check for the underflow computed above. CharAllocator::Erase()
> gains the same check for the container and for the inner list it is
> about to erase from. These are not on a hot path: erasing a quad already
> performs a linear copy of the rest of the inner list.
>
> Bug: 561998123
>

[Sync] Drop getLastUsedRegularProfile in PassphraseDialogFragment

In crrev.com/c/5350138 (March 2024), PassphraseDialogFragment was
updated to retrieve its Profile from PassphraseDialogFragment.Delegate,
accompanied by an assert and a temporary fallback to
ProfileManager.getLastUsedRegularProfile() with a TODO(crbug.com/327687076)
to remove the fallback once verified that the assert does not fire.

Crash telemetry since M124 shows 0 triggers of this assert across Canary
and Dev channels (the same assert produced 11 Canary crashes in
PassphraseDialogFragment.getPromptText before crrev.com/c/5350138, none
since), and all three Delegate implementations (ManageSyncSettings,
AccountManagementFragment, and PassphraseActivity) initialize their
Profile prior to FragmentActivity.onStart() when
DialogFragment.onCreateDialog() executes. Remove the deprecated ambient
profile fallback.

Crash telemetry evidence (Googlers only): go/clank-mp-crash-evidence

[Omnibox] Re-enable AIM eligibility service browser tests

In `ChromeAimEligibilityServiceBrowserTest`,
`ComprehensiveEligibilityTest` was disabled on Linux dbg in
https://crrev.com/c/7636971, on Linux release in
https://crrev.com/c/7644074 (https://crbug.com/488467253), and on
Windows ASan in https://crrev.com/c/7897314 due to flakiness.

In `ChromeAimEligibilityServiceStartupRequestBrowserTest`,
`RequestWhenOfflineAtStartup` and `NoRequestOnSubsequentNetworkChanges`
were disabled across platforms in https://crrev.com/c/7403547
(https://crbug.com/473787329) due to a flake rate on Linux and ChromeOS.

In `ChromeAimEligibilityServiceOAuthBrowserTest`,
`OTRRequestIsNotDropped` was disabled across platforms in
https://crrev.com/c/7648648 and https://crrev.com/c/7648910
(https://crbug.com/488467253).

The underlying flakiness across the AIM eligibility browser tests was
caused by a startup race condition where browser profile initialization
instantiated `AimEligibilityService` before test fixtures could
configure `content::URLLoaderInterceptor` or the mock network change
notifier. This race condition was resolved in
https://crrev.com/c/7623216 by introducing `AimEligibilityTestBase`,
which sets a null testing factory during profile setup and defers
`AimEligibilityService` initialization until explicitly requested via
`GetAimEligibilityService()`. Additionally, cookie-based refresh and
OAuth fallback handling were stabilized in https://crrev.com/c/8488286.

This CL removes `BUILDFLAG(IS_LINUX)` from
`MAYBE_ComprehensiveEligibilityTest`, removes the `DISABLED_` prefix
from `RequestWhenOfflineAtStartup` and
`NoRequestOnSubsequentNetworkChanges`, and defines
`MAYBE_OTRRequestIsNotDropped` to keep `OTRRequestIsNotDropped` disabled
on ChromeOS and Mac while re-enabling it on Linux.

Tested on Linux desktop with Xvfb.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

content: Route GpuHostImpl and GPU channel to resize task runner

This CL routes `GpuProcessHost::Init()`, `viz::GpuHostImpl`, and
`BrowserGpuChannelHostFactory::EstablishRequest` through
`BrowserMainLoop::GetResizeTaskRunner()` across all platforms,
preserving macOS behavior while giving non-macOS platforms the same
startup priority routing.

Historically, `viz::GpuHostImpl` and
`BrowserGpuChannelHostFactory::EstablishRequest` only used
`ui::WindowResizeHelperMac::Get()->task_runner()` on macOS so GPU Mojo
replies could be pumped while Cocoa blocked in modal live-resize loops,
while non-macOS platforms used `GetCurrentDefault()` (which was
identical to `BrowserMainLoop::GetResizeTaskRunner()` at the time).

When `kPrioritizeResizeTaskRunnerOnStartup` (crrev.com/c/8133994)
repurposed `BrowserMainLoop::GetResizeTaskRunner()` to route startup
compositor tasks to `BrowserTaskType::kStartup`, macOS automatically
routed `GpuHostImpl` and `EstablishRequest` to `kStartup` because
`WindowResizeHelperMac::Init()` wraps that task runner. On non-macOS
platforms, however, they remained bound to the normal-priority default
UI task runner, queuing `EstablishGpuChannel` replies behind normal UI
startup work.

Local Linux Crossbench `browser-startup` A/B results (32 repetitions per
story, N=96 paired runs across `newtab_startup`, `blank_startup`, and
`google_startup`):
- `Startup.BrowserWindow.FirstPaint`:
  - `newtab_startup`: P50 (median) -23.50 ms (-4.90%),
    95% CI [-36.00, -15.00] ms
  - `blank_startup`: P50 (median) -28.00 ms (-5.81%),
    95% CI [-34.50, -18.00] ms
  - `google_startup`: P50 (median) -32.00 ms (-6.69%),
    95% CI [-48.50, -8.00] ms
  - All stories (N=96): P50 (median) -26.00 ms (-5.42%),
    95% CI [-33.00, -18.00] ms
- `InitialWebUI.Startup.ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint`:
  - All stories (N=96): P50 (median) -7.00 ms (-1.35%),
    95% CI [-19.00, -2.00] ms
- `Startup.FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3`:
  - All stories (N=96): P50 (median) -11.00 ms (-1.74%),
    95% CI [-14.00, -3.00] ms

Disallow stack-allocated types in STL collections in blink_gc_plugin

STACK_ALLOCATED() classes can hold raw pointers to GarbageCollected
objects because conservative stack scanning keeps stack-resident
references alive, and class-specific operator new is deleted. However,
STL containers allocate backing storage on the heap and construct
elements via placement new. This means that storing a STACK_ALLOCATED()
object in a heap-backed STL container places its raw Oilpan pointers on
the heap outside stack scanning, which can cause premature garbage
collection and dangling pointers.

This change extends CollectionOfGarbageCollectedMatcher to flag
STACK_ALLOCATED() types (directly or in std::pair) in std::vector,
std::map, std::unordered_map, std::set, and std::unordered_set.
std::array remains allowed since its elements are stored inline (and
invalid field usage on non-stack classes is already enforced by field
checking), and both GC_PLUGIN_IGNORE and STACK_ALLOCATED_IGNORE are
respected.

The new check is gated behind a default-disabled
enable-off-heap-collections-of-stack-allocated-check plugin flag so it
does not block the Clang roll. Existing violations in the codebase are
suppressed with STACK_ALLOCATED_IGNORE in crrev.com/c/8732462 to allow
this feature to be enabled in a follow-up.

content: Post EstablishRequest retry to main_task_runner_

This CL updates `BrowserGpuChannelHostFactory::EstablishRequest` to post
its `Establish()` retry task to `main_task_runner_` instead of
`GetUIThreadTaskRunner({})` when `OnEstablished()` receives
`kGpuHostInvalid`.

Before `kProcessHostOnUI` (crrev.com/c/2806425 and crrev.com/c/3178241),
`EstablishOnIO()` ran on the IO thread while `RestartTimeout()` ran on
`main_task_runner_` (the UI thread). When `EstablishRequest` was
migrated to the UI thread, `GetIOThreadTaskRunner({})` was mechanically
replaced with `GetUIThreadTaskRunner({})` instead of reusing
`main_task_runner_`.

[bookmarks] Preallocate vectors with known sizes

- Reserve capacity upfront in BookmarkRemoteUpdatesHandler,
  BookmarkEventTranslator, and BookmarksServiceImpl where output vector
  sizes are known before population, avoiding repeated reallocations
  over large bookmark collections.
- Replace manual push_back conversion and event-cloning loops in
  components/browser_apis/bookmarks with base::ToVector.
- These were reported as some of the potentially largest vectors in the
  Chromium codebase, peaking at 100,000+ elements, so reserving capacity
  can save up to 18 reallocations.

[infra] Increase interactive_ui_tests shards on mac-no-initial-webui-rel

interactive_ui_tests on mac-no-initial-webui-rel fails because its
shards hit the 60 minute swarming timeout. In
https://ci.chromium.org/b/8665876171907071681 (build 5856), shards #2
and #3 timed out both in the original run and in the retry.

The suite runs on only 4 shards, and its total runtime is about 231
minutes, so each shard takes about 53-60 minutes. That leaves no
headroom under the 60 minute timeout.

Raise the shard count from 4 to 8. Each shard should then take about
30 minutes. This is in line with other Mac-26 testers, e.g.
mac-separate-renderer-fyi-rel (8) and mac26-arm64-rel-tests (16).

[AW] Re-enable DeveloperUiTest on non-automotive devices

`DeveloperUiTest` test suite was unconditionally disabled in
https://crrev.com/c/5923540 for Buganizer issue 369532182 due to
flakiness. In https://crrev.com/c/5983939, it was partially re-enabled,
and the author's stated intention was to restrict the flaky tests
strictly to non-automotive devices. However, the `@DisabledTest`
annotation was incorrectly applied unconditionally again instead of
using `DeviceRestriction`.

This CL replaces the unconditional `@DisabledTest` annotations with
`@Restriction({DeviceRestriction.RESTRICTION_TYPE_NON_AUTO})` to
correctly implement the intended automotive-only restriction and
re-enable the tests on non-automotive devices. Verified on Android
API levels 31 through 36 using AVD emulators for both phone and tablet
form factors, as well as foldable devices.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

Wait for BookmarkModel load in SignInAndEnableAccountBookmarkNodes

`SignInAndEnableAccountBookmarkNodes` calls
`BookmarkModel::CreateAccountPermanentFolders()`, which `CHECK`s that
`BookmarkModel` has finished loading (`CHECK(loaded_)`). In
`BookmarkMessageHandlerAccountAwarePromoTest.*`, signing in immediately
on test startup can race async bookmark model loading and crash.

Wait for `BookmarkModel` to finish loading via
`bookmarks::test::WaitForBookmarkModelToLoad()` before creating account
permanent folders.

https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Abrowser_tests%21gtest%3A%3ABookmarkMessageHandlerAccountAwarePromoTest%23MaxShownCountLimit

[TabGroupSync] Batch storage updates in local tab group mutations

Wraps LocalTabGroupMutationHelper createNewTabGroup and reconcileGroup
in a ScopedStorageBatch via TabStateStorageServiceFactory.createBatch.
When syncing large tab groups (e.g. 250+ tabs), this coalesces all
background tab creations, group merges, and visual updates into a
single atomic storage transaction, preventing hundreds of unbatched
disk writes.

[TabStateStore] Preserve TabState and freeze tabs on fallback

In TabRestorer.maybeRestoreTab, when tabState.contentsState is null
but tabState.url is non-null, synthesize a single-navigation
WebContentsState via
WebContentsState.createSingleNavigationWebContentsState.

This ensures the tab restores as a frozen tab via createFrozenTab,
preserving tabGroupId, tabId, and isPinned rather than discarding
all TabState metadata and falling back to createTabWithoutContentsState.
If WebContentsState synthesis fails or returns an empty buffer, it
gracefully falls back to createTabWithoutContentsState.

[iOS] Remove pref observers in `GeminiServiceImpl::Shutdown()`

`GeminiServiceImpl::Shutdown()` did not reset `pref_change_registrar_`,
retaining a pointer to `PrefService` until destruction rather than
releasing it in `Shutdown()`.

While it does not seems to actually be an issue, due to the order on
service, it’s still better practice for service to stop depending on
each other at shutdown time.

The observation was added in https://crrev.com/c/7957429. That CL does
not seem to indicate why it was not reset in `Shutdown()`.

[GPU] Re-enable `GLCubeMapTextureTest` pixel readback tests

`GLCubeMapTextureTest.ReadPixels` and
`GLCubeMapTextureTest.ReadPixelsFromIncompleteCubeTexture` were disabled
due to flakiness observed specifically on ASan/LSan builders
(https://crbug.com/40246425).

The tests verify reading pixels from framebuffer attachments backed by
complete and incomplete cube map textures.

Guarding the tests with `#if defined(ADDRESS_SANITIZER) &&
defined(LEAK_SANITIZER)` mirrors the existing pattern used for
`MAYBE_Compositor` in `gl_bind_uniform_location_unittest.cc`, allowing
the tests to run on macOS, Linux, and other standard configurations
while keeping ASan/LSan disabled until the sanitizer issues are
resolved.

Local verification on macOS and Linux confirms that both tests execute
deterministically without failures.

This CL introduces `MAYBE_ReadPixels` and
`MAYBE_ReadPixelsFromIncompleteCubeTexture`, and adds documentation
comments.

Verified on macOS.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

parent
03f931d3ccf3cf162673423c21ab8182bfa93d94 [ diff ] 
[CCT] Cancel cookie-restore callback when tab controller is destroyed

When an Off-The-Record Custom Tab restores cipher data via
CookiesFetcher.restoreCookies(), the asynchronous callback can run after
the CustomTabActivity has been destroyed. finishTabInitializationPostNative()
then created and attached a new OTR Tab after
BaseCustomTabActivity.destroyTabModels() and
CustomTabIncognitoManager.onDestroy() had already run, leaking the OTR
WebContents past OTR Profile destruction.

Wrap the callback in a CallbackController and cancel it in destroy(), so
no tab is created once the controller is torn down.

[TTC] Unify how session updates reach the UI

The TTC session used to send audio levels, errors, transcripts and the
backend connecting to its UI through dedicated calls, while everything
else followed it as an observer. The UI is now an observer too,
registered by the session when it's created, and works out what to show
from the session's lifecycle. On Android, it forwards these updates to
the Java bridge, which no longer observes the session itself.

[TabUI] Decouple CloseAllTabsHelper from ArchivedTabModelOrchestrator

CloseAllTabsHelper previously reached directly into
ArchivedTabModelOrchestrator and TabArchiver through a DEPS exemption,
blocking modularization out of chrome_java and bypassing lifecycle and
lease protections during undo. Moving the archived-tab handling onto
ArchivedTabModelOrchestrator and injecting a Supplier<Runnable> removes
the dependency and prepares CloseAllTabsHelper for modularization into
chrome/browser/tab_ui/android.

Expose whether an image contains an embedded C2PA manifest in Annotated
Page Content (APC).

unsupported for the image format (C2PAManifestStatus::kUnknown), the
field is left unset.

[blink] Clean up BucketFileSystemBuilder handle lifetime and AsBlob

Follow-up improvements to BucketFileSystemBuilder:
1. Keep the input FileSystemDirectoryHandle alive via a traced
   Member<FileSystemDirectoryHandle> directory_handle_ on
   BucketFileSystemBuilder while GetEntries() is in flight so GC does
   not collect the handle and close its HeapMojoRemote prematurely.
2. Add BucketFileSystemBuilder::Dispose() and call it from
   BucketFileSystemAgent::Dispose() and on builder completion to
   deterministically close the Mojo receiver and release handles.
3. Bind BucketFileSystemBuilder::DidBuildFile() directly to AsBlob()
   instead of wrapping it in an intermediate lambda. This also fixes
   error handling in DidBuildFile() where checking !file before
   result->status != kOk previously made
   BucketFileSystemAgent::HandleError() unreachable on AsBlob() errors.

Reapply "IDB: add metrics to determine ideal db close grace period in SQLite"

This reverts commit 666bcdd1ebf847d3a67e0d89a882fa55453ea3ab.

The flaky test is fixed by replacing `RunUntil` (which was waiting for a
wakeup that didn't come for 30 seconds at times) with a `ForceClose`
with `RunLoop`.

Original change's description:
> IDB: add metrics to determine ideal db close grace period in SQLite
>
> LevelDB is unaffected.
>
> ConnectionDestructionGracePeriodWasUseful logs a binary result for
> whether the destruction grace period successfully allowed a subsequent
> connection to reuse a hot DatabaseConnection.
>
> ConnectionReopenedAfterDestruction tells us how long it's been since the
> database was last open. (Nothing is logged if it wasn't previously
> opened.) This gives us an understanding of how much longer than 2s we'd
> have to extend the grace period to capture more reopen cases.
>
> Aside from collecting data, there are two slight behavioral changes:
>
> 1. In-memory DBs are closed (or not) without using the grace period
>    (this frees memory slightly faster after an in-memory db is deleted)
> 2. An empty backing store is kept around for a full 3 minutes for
>    SQLite, which should have little to no functional impact since the
>    backing store doesn't hold onto files or much in the way of memory.
>    This is necessary for the new metrics to work.
>

[omnibox][webui] Re-enable WebUI omnibox in toolbar tests

These tests disabled kWebUIOmniboxPopup and kWebUIOmniboxAimPopup as a
temporary workaround when the features were enabled by default
(crrev.com/c/8092074). The failures came from the hidden WebUI popup
WebContents that every browser window used to create at startup.
InProcessBrowserTest now creates those popups on demand
(crrev.com/c/8647556), so the overrides are no longer needed.

Verified with a CQ dry run of all such removals together
(crrev.com/c/8728211) and local repeat runs comparing the features
enabled vs. disabled, which showed no difference in failure rates.

[GEiC] Narrow guest URL allowlist to exact hostnames

Per Chrome Security review, replace the wildcard gemini.google /
gemini.google.com domain checks and the Finch kGeicGuestURL host check
in IsAllowedGeminiEnterpriseHost() with tiered host validation:

- Policy: an explicit list of exact production Gemini Enterprise
  hostnames, with no wildcards.
- Finch: policy hosts plus pre-production and internal corp hosts,
  matched by product-prefixed patterns limited to a single DNS label
  (e.g. business-<label>.gemini.google, ucs-<label>.corp.google.com).
- --geic-guest-url (also settable from chrome://flags): Finch hosts plus
  HTTP or HTTPS localhost for local development and browser tests.

All sources must be HTTPS (except localhost) and free of embedded
credentials. Adding a host or widening a pattern requires a Chrome
Security review. --glic-dev no longer relaxes these checks.

[FSA] Fix FilePathWatcher kqueue and FSEvents event coalescing on Mac

This CL fixes two causes of spurious FilePathWatcher events on macOS 26:

1. In `FilePathWatcherKQueue::EventsForPath()`, only subscribe to
   `NOTE_ATTRIB` on ancestor directories (where `subdir` is non-empty
   and `HandleAttributesChange()` checks whether the child path
   component became inaccessible), omitting `NOTE_ATTRIB` on the target
   entry itself. Attribute-only changes on the watched target are not
   supposed to trigger notifications, and macOS 26 emits delayed
   background `NOTE_ATTRIB` events on newly written or moved files.

2. In `FilePathWatcherFSEventsChangeTracker::DispatchEvents()`, update
   the local `coalesce_target_creation` and `coalesce_target_deletion`
   flags when `kFSEventStreamEventFlagRootChanged` is processed, and
   check for coalesced target creation before checking for
   `ItemInodeMetaMod | ItemModified` so that target creation events
   carrying `ItemCreated | ItemModified | ItemInodeMetaMod` are
   coalesced after `RootChanged`.

[TabStateStore] Extract WebContentsState for lazy tabs

In TabStoragePackagerAndroid::Package, when web_contents() is null
or fails to serialize, or when the tab has pending load params,
request WebContentsState extraction from Java via
TabStoragePackager.fetchTabStorageMetadata.

This extracts the serialized WebContentsState via TabStateExtractor,
passing both its buffer and saved state version dynamically across
JNI to populate web_contents_state_bytes and version without
hardcoding version constants.
